By: Aaron Hermes   
 June 24th, 2026

We’ve gone through a bit of an evolution lately here at Interloc. Our flagship product, Mobile Informer, was getting a long in the tooth. First introduced in 2010, Mobile Informer had provided innovative mobile applications for Maximo to customers around the world for a decade and a half. In that time, IBM had introduced several new versions of Maximo, culminating with the release (in June 2020) of the Maximo Application Suite (MAS). Officially version 8.0, the name change from Maximo EAM to MAS reflected a renewed commitment to advancing the capabilities of the solution, including a significant change to the underlying infrastructure involved.

# Interloc Solutions Launches interloc.ai, AI Agents Built for IBM Maximo Asset Management

### Key Takeaways

#### Model Release

IBM Maximo is enterprise asset management software used by large industrial, utilities, and facilities organizations to track equipment, schedule maintenance, and manage work orders. It’s not a consumer product, it’s the system a refinery or a hospital network uses to know when a pump needs servicing. Interloc Solutions, a company that builds Maximo-focused software, now says it’s added an agentic AI layer on top: interloc.ai. [...] The catch is that everything above comes from Interloc itself. The PRNewswire release is down, and no independent editorial coverage of this launch was available at publication. What’s confirmed: the company exists, the product launched, and Interloc’s own website and a Yahoo Finance aggregation of the press release carry consistent descriptions of the platform. What isn’t confirmed: whether the agent architecture performs as described, what the actual integration complexity looks like, or how the human-in-the-loop controls behave at scale.
